evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 男; 形義通解; 字形与例证
evidence.text: The entry reports oracle-bone and bronze forms built from 田 and 力; it interprets 力 as a plough-like implement and attributes the explanation that the combination represents working a field, later used for a male person, to Xu Zhongshu. It separately reports oracle-bone use as 男服; bronze uses for 男服/rank in 令方彝, a male-person use in 齊侯盤, a son use in 翏生盨, and a personal name. These are source-reported readings and uses; they do not by themselves establish a complete chronological semantic chain.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: 普及版 字通, via Kotobank
evidence.text: This dictionary classifies 男 as 田 + 力, interpreting 力 as a plough (耒) and the graph as cultivation, with an early referent it describes as a land manager. It cites 令彝 for a rank/domain use. This is a dictionary interpretation of the graph and inscription, not a directly demonstrated pictorial identification or uncontested semantic sequence.
evidence.title: 男(オトコ)とは？ 意味や使い方 - コトバンク

evidence.source: 普及版 字通, via Kotobank
evidence.field: 男の語誌; dated Japanese word attestations
evidence.text: The dictionary describes Japanese おとこ as originally referring to a young adult male and as already contrasting with をみな in ancient usage. Its dated examples elsewhere on the page include Kojiki (712), Nihon Shoki (720), Man'yōshū (8th century), and Tosa Nikki (c. 935). These attestations concern Japanese vocabulary and do not date the origin or semantic development of the Chinese graph 男.
evidence.title: 男(オトコ)とは？ 意味や使い方 - コトバンク

evidence.field: File description; summary, original-file link and licensing
evidence.text: The inspected description identifies the file as a vector depiction of 男 in Shang oracle-script style, gives the source glyph as Xiaoxuetang record 43.F356 (京津2122 合3457), and links the original SVG. It explicitly identifies a digital vector creation, not an artifact photograph, and states CC0/public-domain reuse. The browser exposed the actual original-file URL through the inspected page, although fetching its bytes returned a cache-miss error.

gaps: Individual oracle and bronze artifact images and inscription contexts were not independently inspected; the form/use descriptions here remain attributed to the scholarly database and dictionaries.
The sources report both an early rank/domain use and uses for male person and son, but do not establish a dated semantic bridge or an uncontested order for these senses.

The plough-like interpretation of 力 is a scholarly/dictionary account. No independent ancient name or pronunciation of the depicted implement was established; this is not evidence for a whole-graph phonetic loan.

Modern readings and reconstruction comparisons were not re-queried in this verification pass; the dossier's local Baxter–Sagart cross-check does not support 力 as a phonetic component, and neither component is proposed here as a sound component.

The Xiaoxuetang direct glyph image URL returned a cache-miss fetch failure. The Commons vector's original-file link was verified on the exact file page, but media bytes were also inaccessible to this browser. No image was visually inspected in this research pass.
No versioned local corpus extract is recommended: the inspected character-specific pages and image rights information suffice for this entry, and no bulk reuse permission was established.

items.period: Shang period oracle-bone script (file description's script designation; source form identified as record 43.F356)
items.caption: A modern vector redraw of a Shang oracle-script form of 男, linked by its file description to Xiaoxuetang record 43.F356 (京津2122 / 合3457).
items.alt: Vector outline of an oracle-script glyph identified as 男.
items.selection_reason: A character-specific source record and file description identify the form and its provenance; useful as a candidate illustration of the early graph. It is a redraw, not an ancient artifact photograph, and its pixels were not inspected in this pass.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 / public domain as stated on the exact Commons file description page; source Xiaoxuetang query-interface glyph image and glyph attributes also covered by the official CC0 notice.

limitations.text: The direct Xiaoxuetang glyph-image request and Commons original media fetch both failed in the browser with cache-miss errors; the candidate is supported by the inspected descriptions and provenance, not visual inspection.
